lesson: In merge_tags, union sources in precedence order and deduplicate case-insensitively while preserving the casing and ordering of the first occurrence, never lowercasing the output.
why: The Terraform provider treats casing as significant and saved searches require exact casing matches.
quote: Never lowercase — the Terraform provider treats casing as significant and our saved searches match exact casing. Keep the casing of the first occurrence

lesson: In merge_tags, collect all dash-prefixed entries into a global kill list to strip those tags case-insensitively from the final output, never outputting literal dash tags and silently ignoring unmatched entries.
why: Dash entries represent deliberate deletions by ops, and unmatched removals occur speculatively and must not wedge the sync.
quote: an entry that matches nothing is silently fine — ops writes them speculatively, erroring would wedge the sync.

lesson: In tag-merge processing, replace the rejected global kill list rule with downward-only suppression, so a tombstone only suppresses matching tags from lower-precedence sources and never deletes tags asserted by higher-precedence sources.
why: A low-precedence legacy inventory sync emitted '-compliance:sox', erroneously deleting a CMDB-asserted compliance tag on production hosts and triggering a 2am audit alert.
quote: A '-name' tombstone suppresses that tag, matched case-insensitively, from LOWER-precedence sources only; it never removes a tag a higher-precedence source asserted itself.
